rulings.challenge_claim: Onset, marks and frame check out, but (1) a byte-true catchword straddles the row's own 66:4|66:5 rear seam undisclosed, (2) one signal key names a divine-title class the cited verse's bytes do not carry, and (3) the unit's characterization leans on the rendering's supplied comparative at 66:3 where the Hebrew juxtaposes bare participles.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes; MT 66 is outside both offset zones, so identity numbering holds and no dual-cite is owed anywhere in this ruling. Defect 1 UPHELD. The row's span-internal MT 66:2 closes וְחָרֵ֖ד עַל דְּבָרִֽי (byte tier) and the next unit's opener MT 66:5 carries הַחֲרֵדִ֖ים אֶל דְּבָר֑וֹ (byte tier): the trembler-plus-word pairing sits on both sides of this row's own rear seam and names the following unit's addressees from inside this one. The count-object re-derives exactly as the challenge names it — the trembling root stands in 7 verses book-wide (sweep: 7 verses at MT 10:29, 19:16, 21:4, 32:11, 41:5, 66:2, 66:5, skeleton tier), MT 66:2/66:5 being its only chapter sites and its only adjacent pair. The standing cross-seam rule makes a byte-true device across the row's own seam an argument for continuity unless disclosed, and no field of the row discloses it. The cut itself is untouched: the verse-initial imperative שִׁמְעוּ֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier) stands as tokens 1-3 of MT 66:5, and the tier-3 single-witness paragraph-mark inventory records SAMEKH at MT 66:4 and MT 65:25, correctly typed, with 0 PE anywhere in the chapter (chapter marks: SAMEKH at MT 66:4, 66:9, 66:11; nearest PE at MT 65:12) — all as the row states. Defect 2 UPHELD. MT 66:1 reads כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם כִּסְאִ֔י וְהָאָ֖רֶץ הֲדֹ֣ם רַגְלָ֑י (byte tier): the throne/footstool line is two verbless self-predications, and the verse's only divine-title-class token is the tetragrammaton already carried by the frame key. The second signal key therefore asserts a signal class the cited site's bytes do not instantiate, and double-counts the one title token it could reach. Defect 3 REFUTED. The row's clause is a verbatim rendering quote carrying its own inline reference in the same field — “He who kills an ox is as he who kills a man” (web:Isa.66.3) reproduces the rendering exactly to its clause end — so the sanctioned quote convention is met, and the comparative belongs to the rendering the row cites, not to a Hebrew claim the row makes. The construal is also not load-bearing: the boundary rests on the frame onset and the rear-seam imperative, and the unit's judgment character is carried by the verse's own second half, גַּם הֵ֗מָּה בָּֽחֲרוּ֙ בְּדַרְכֵיהֶ֔ם וּבְשִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֖ם נַפְשָׁ֥ם חָפֵֽצָה (byte tier), which condemns without any comparative particle. Register-level strictness, not a defect.
rulings.remedy: Two edits, no boundary change. (a) boundary_rationale (or device_notes): add ONE sentence disclosing the cross-seam trembler-plus-word catchword, splicing the pointed forms from MT 66:2 and MT 66:5, naming the tier and the swept object with its digit (trembling root, sweep: 7 verses, skeleton tier), and stating that the cut still stands on the verse-initial imperative at MT 66:5 plus the tier-3 single-witness SAMEKH at MT 66:4. TEST the cure must pass: a cross-seam-cohesion read of the finished row finds the device disclosed, every added Hebrew run re-collates at byte tier against the verse it is cited to, and the digit names both its object and its unit. (b) observed_substrate_signals: replace the divine-title key with a dotted key naming a class MT 66:1's bytes actually instantiate (the divine self-predication under an oracle_frame.* key); do not re-file it under a divine-title class. TEST: every key in the field resolves to a signal instantiated in the row's own span bytes, and no single token is claimed by two keys.

rulings.challenge_claim: The rival cut at 66:5|66:6 is rejected on an absence claim the bytes contradict: MT 66:6 is a verse-initial threefold herald-voice verse with a change of grammatical person.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes. The rejected-alternative field declines the 66:5|66:6 cut on the ground that 'no tier-1 addressee or frame shift divides them'. Both halves of that absence fail at the named seam. MT 66:6 opens ק֤וֹל שָׁאוֹן֙ מֵעִ֔יר (byte tier) as tokens 1-3 and stacks three herald-voice tokens across its 10 tokens; a verse-initial herald-voice opener stands in exactly 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses at MT 13:4, 40:3, 40:6, 52:8, 66:6, skeleton tier) — my own sweep returns that list unchanged, and the object matches the digit (first-token identity, not a substring anywhere in the verse, which would return 31 verses). Two of those five sites are the herald openers the frame spine itself classes as tier-1 scene-shift signals where explicit in the bytes, so this is not a signal class the row may treat as absent. The person shift is byte-true as well: MT 66:5 governs its addressees in the second person (הַחֲרֵדִ֖ים אֶל דְּבָר֑וֹ, byte tier) and MT 66:6 reports in the third throughout. The boundary is NOT contested and is not in play: the onset שִׁמְעוּ֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה (byte tier) is verse-initial masculine-plural imperative, and the tier-3 single-witness inventory carries SAMEKH at MT 66:4 and MT 66:9, correctly typed, with no PE, no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note in MT 66:5-9, so span-relevant disclosure is complete. The defect is confined to the stated ground of a mandated field.
rulings.remedy: One edit to strongest_rejected_alternative, boundary unchanged. Replace the absence ground with a ground the bytes support: if the 66:5|66:6 cut is still declined, decline it because the herald-voice verse reports the recompense the summons announces and remains inside the same summons unit — and acknowledge in the same sentence the verse-initial herald-voice opener at MT 66:6 (sweep: 5 verses book-wide, skeleton tier) and the second-to-third person shift. TEST the cure must pass: no absence claim left in the field survives a byte check at the seam it names, and the rival's replacement ground is itself falsifiable from the bytes and survives that test. Same edit, optional strengthening the row already owes: MT 66:9 ends verse-finally with the Elohim variant of the postpositive speech signature, אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ (byte tier), which the row carries only in rendering; name it as the closure signal it is, with the position byte-checked (verse-final, no dividing accent on the final token). TEST: any closure claim states position verified against token order and accent, not asserted.

rulings.challenge_claim: The retention argument mislabels the unit's rear-seam signal as an imperative onset, and the suckle catchword crossing that same seam is disclosed only in translation.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes; both defects hold. Defect 1: device_notes grounds retention on 'the tier-1 imperative-onset signals on either side of it', but the rear side is MT 66:12, which opens כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (byte tier) and carries no imperative among its 20 tokens — its finite forms are a presentative plus participle and three imperfect/consecutive forms. The label also contradicts the row's own boundary_rationale, which correctly calls MT 66:12 a messenger frame. The front-side label is byte-true: שִׂמְח֧וּ אֶת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם (byte tier) is verse-initial and one of three imperatives in MT 66:10. Defect 2: תִּֽינְקוּ֙ (MT 66:11, byte tier) and וִֽינַקְתֶּ֑ם (MT 66:12, byte tier) put the same suckle root on both sides of the row's rear seam, and the rejected-alternative field discloses that tie only as English nursing-and-comfort imagery, with no pointed form and no tier label, where a boundary-relevant cohesion claim owes both. The challenge's count-object is right and its trap-handling is right: the attested suckle-family sites are MT 60:16 (וְיָנַקְתְּ֙, byte tier), 66:11 and 66:12 — 3 verses, skeleton tier — while a bare three-letter substring returns 4 verses, the fourth being MT 29:1, whose יִנְקֹֽפוּ belongs to a different root. Neither defect touches the boundary: the rear seam stands on the messenger frame at MT 66:12, and the tier-3 single-witness inventory carries SAMEKH at MT 66:9 and MT 66:11, correctly typed, with no PE, paseq or ketiv/qere note in MT 66:10-11.
rulings.remedy: Two edits, no boundary change. (a) device_notes: correct the form-class label — the rear-side signal at MT 66:12 is a messenger-frame onset, not an imperative onset; keep the front-side imperative label, which the bytes carry. TEST the cure must pass: every form-class label in the row is byte-checkable against the token list of the verse it is cited to, and no label contradicts the row's own boundary_rationale. (b) strongest_rejected_alternative: re-cut the merge-forward rival so the nursing ground carries the pointed suckle forms spliced from MT 66:11 and MT 66:12 with the tier named, and cites the swept object with its digit and its trap exclusion (suckle family, sweep: 3 verses at MT 60:16 / 66:11 / 66:12, skeleton tier; a bare three-letter substring returns 4 verses, one of them a different root). TEST: the boundary-relevant cohesion claim carries a pointed splice plus a tier label, and the digit names its object and excludes the short-token trap site.

rulings.challenge_claim: LF (low): device_notes mischaracterizes the 65:17/66:22 new-heavens relationship as a skeleton-tier recurrence when direct collation returns no match at any tier, and the signal key borrows the refrain namespace for a looser echo. OL (medium): four defects — the postpositive signature at MT 66:22 stands mid-verse at the major divider rather than sealing the unit; the verse-final signature at MT 66:21 sits inside the span undisclosed and against the row's own rival ground; the recurrence tier is overstated; and the paseq disclosure at MT 66:20 understates the inventory count.
rulings.grounds: CONVERGENCE: LF's single item and OL's third defect are the SAME defect (the recurrence-tier overstatement); OL's first, second and fourth defects are DISTINCT and LF did not reach them. All four re-derive from bytes; the corrected finding is a four-defect item at medium, so LF's severity understates the row's defect load, while OL's headline ('the closing warrant is byte-false') is right about the sealing clause but overstates the reach: the row's operative rear-seam ground — that MT 66:23 opens a recurring-time formula rather than continuing the ingathering — is untouched, as is the span. Defect 1 UPHELD. MT 66:22 runs 17 tokens; נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה stands as tokens 12-13, its divine-name token carrying the verse's major dividing accent (etnahta, U+0591), with four tokens following — כֵּ֛ן יַעֲמֹ֥ד זַרְעֲכֶ֖ם וְשִׁמְכֶֽם — that complete the comparison opened by כִּ֣י כַאֲשֶׁ֣ר. The rendering sets the same clause mid-sentence, so both witnesses agree against the row's 'sealed by the closing signature'. Contrast MT 66:17, where the pair נְאֻם יְהוָֽה is genuinely verse-final and its last token carries only a meteg, no dividing accent. The row's splice itself re-collates at byte tier — the defect is positional, not copy-degradation. Defect 2 UPHELD. MT 66:21 is a complete clause, וְגַם מֵהֶ֥ם אֶקַּ֛ח לַכֹּהֲנִ֥ים לַלְוִיִּ֖ם אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (byte tier), terminated verse-finally by אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה; the contiguous speech-signature pair stands in 53 verses book-wide and is verse-final in only 5 (sweep: 5 verses at MT 39:6, 54:1, 65:25, 66:21, 66:23, skeleton tier) — my sweep returns that list unchanged. Two of the five are in this chapter and one falls inside this row's span, undisclosed, while the rejected-alternative field declines the 66:21 cut precisely on the ground that no tier-1 shift divides it: a closure-class signal of the very class the row invokes elsewhere is the evidence that ground had to answer. NEW FINDING (peer-added; neither primary reached it): a third signature, אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (byte tier), stands mid-verse at the etnahta inside MT 66:20 — the row engages none of the three speech signatures its own span carries. Defect 3 UPHELD (both sources). MT 65:17 reads שָׁמַ֥יִם חֲדָשִׁ֖ים וָאָ֣רֶץ חֲדָשָׁ֑ה (indefinite) and MT 66:22 הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם הַ֠חֳדָשִׁים וְהָאָ֨רֶץ הַחֲדָשָׁ֜ה (definite, article on both nouns and both adjectives); collating the MT 66:22 four-token run against MT 65:17 returns tier none, and the reverse direction returns tier none, so the label 'skeleton-tier recurrence' is unsupportable. Each four-token string stands in exactly 1 verse book-wide (sweep: 1 verse each, skeleton tier) and even their two-token pairs do not cross. The link is a lexical collocation differing in determination, and the refrain-namespace signal key inherits the same overstatement. Defect 4 UPHELD, at the low end. The tier-3 single-witness count-layer inventory records 2 paseq segs at MT 66:20 and 1 at MT 66:19; the row annotates both refs with the same singular wording, understating the MT 66:20 count. No PE or SAMEKH falls in MT 66:18-22 and none is claimed — correctly disclosed — and no ketiv/qere note stands in the span.
rulings.remedy: Four edits; the span is NOT changed by any of them. (a) boundary_rationale: delete the 'sealed by the closing signature' clause and restate the rear-seam ground on what the bytes carry; if the postpositive pair at MT 66:22 is retained at all, describe it as standing mid-verse at the major divider inside the unfinished comparison. TEST the cure must pass: every position word ('closing', 'final', 'sealed') is verified against token order AND accent for the verse cited, and against both witnesses' renderings — the test that killed the original. (b) strongest_rejected_alternative: disclose the verse-final speech signature terminating MT 66:21 (sweep: 53 verses total / 5 verse-final, skeleton tier) and give a byte-supported reason for declining the 66:20|66:21 cut, replacing the running-sentence-sequence ground, which the completeness of MT 66:21 and the fresh comparative onset of MT 66:22 contradict. TEST: the rival's replacement ground survives a byte check at the seam it names, and no closure-class signal inside the span is left unweighed. NOTE: actually moving the 66:20|66:21 or 66:21|66:22 seam is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit boss adoption — it is not author work and this remedy does not order it. (c) device_notes and observed_substrate_signals: drop the skeleton-tier recurrence label for the 65:17-to-66:22 new-heavens link, re-describe it as a lexical collocation with different determination, and re-key the refrain.* signal to a class that matches. TEST: any recurrence label is backed by a collation at the tier named (direct collation of the MT 66:22 four-token run against MT 65:17 must return the tier claimed; it returns none). (d) boundary_evidence_refs: correct the MT 66:20 paseq annotation to the inventory count (2 segs; MT 66:19 carries 1), count-only, no intra-verse position asserted. TEST: every count-layer disclosure carries that verse's inventory digit.

rulings.challenge_claim: The couplet's internal turn falls on one of the book's five verse-final speech signatures, which the row neither quotes nor weighs; the byte-level tie arguing for holding the couplet together is likewise uncited; and the front seam offers no tier-1 signal while the rival grounds retention on an unresolved scholarly question.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes; all three defects hold, and none of them decides the held coda-versus-close question — this ruling does not decide it either. Defect 1. MT 66:23 ends אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה verse-finally (byte tier; final token carries a meteg only, no dividing accent), and the contiguous speech-signature pair is verse-final in only 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses at MT 39:6, 54:1, 65:25, 66:21, 66:23, skeleton tier) — my sweep returns that list unchanged. It stands exactly at the internal turn on which the row's terminal-unit decision rests, and the row's rendering quote of 66:23 stops one clause short of it, so the byte evidence bearing most directly on the held question is neither cited nor weighed. Defect 2. The tie running the other way is uncited too: the all-flesh collocation stands at MT 66:23 (כָל בָּשָׂ֛ר, byte tier) and verse-finally at MT 66:24 (לְכָל בָּשָֽׂר, byte tier), with the chapter's third site at MT 66:16 (כָּל בָּשָׂ֑ר, byte tier) — sweep: 3 verses in this chapter, skeleton tier, as the challenge states. NEW FINDING (peer-added scope digit): the same collocation stands in 6 verses book-wide (MT 22:13, 40:5, 49:26, 66:16, 66:23, 66:24, skeleton tier), so the cure must name the scope of whichever digit it cites. The held item is left with byte evidence on neither side. Defect 3. MT 66:23 opens וְהָיָ֗ה (byte tier), a connective-prefixed temporal continuation and not a frame, vocative, imperative or superscription onset; NEW FINDING (peer-added digit the challenge asserted without one): verse-initial instances of that opener stand in 50 verses book-wide (sweep: 50 verses, skeleton tier), so it distinguishes nothing at this seam. No tier-1 onset is therefore argued for the 66:22|66:23 cut, and terminality — correctly noted for the rear — is not a warrant for a front seam. The rejected-alternative field then grounds the retention partly on an unresolved scholarly question, where extra-textual scholarly debate is metadata carrying no boundary authority in this book; holding the question is right, grounding a cut on it is not. Verified correct in the row: the mark statements hold — no PE or SAMEKH at MT 66:22-24, the chapter's only marks being SAMEKH at MT 66:4, 66:9 and 66:11 (tier-3, single-witness), with no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note in the closing span — and both Hebrew splices re-collate at byte tier.
rulings.remedy: Three edits; span, medium_low confidence and frontier flag all unchanged, and the coda-versus-close question stays HELD and undecided. (a) boundary_rationale: extend the rendering quote of 66:23 through its final clause instead of truncating it, and cite plus weigh the verse-final speech signature at MT 66:23 (sweep: 53 verses total / 5 verse-final, skeleton tier) as the byte fact standing at the internal turn the row identifies — weigh it, do not resolve it. TEST the cure must pass: every curly-quoted rendering run is verbatim to its clause end with an inline web: ref in the same field, and no byte-level signal at the row's own identified turn is left uncited. (b) device_notes: cite the all-flesh collocation across the couplet with pointed splices and tiers (MT 66:23 and verse-final at MT 66:24, chapter's third site MT 66:16; sweep: 3 verses in this chapter, 6 book-wide, skeleton tier), so the held question carries byte evidence on both sides. TEST: the held item names the byte evidence bearing on it on BOTH sides, and every digit names its object, its unit and its scope. (c) strongest_rejected_alternative: remove the extra-textual scholarly-debate ground entirely and re-ground the front seam from Isaiah's own text — or state honestly that MT 66:22|66:23 rests on a content distinction because the opener at MT 66:23 is a connective-prefixed temporal continuation attested verse-initially in 50 verses book-wide (skeleton tier), which is why the row sits at reduced confidence. TEST: no field grounds a boundary on extra-textual scholarship, every onset claim names the form and its book-wide frequency, and the frontier disclosure still declines to adjudicate the coda question.
